quest.title: Slumbering Roots
quest.description: Arakunti has headed to the Grove of Dreams, where a way to enter dreams is said to reside. However, the twisting roots of the great tree make finding Aranara — or anything else there really — a taxing task and then some...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x250, Primogem x30, Mora x30000, Hero's Wit x3

talks.objective: Head to the Grove of Dreams to find Arakunti
Play the Rhythm of the Great Dream at the designated location to lure the Aranara out

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh! We finally found you! You're Arakunti, aren't you?

dialogues.speaker: Arakunti
dialogues.text: One might not be.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? What do you mean by that?

dialogues.speaker: Arakunti
dialogues.text: Because one might be a tree, or rain, or a dream of Vana, or the strings of a musical instrument.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Paimon didn't understand a word of what he just said! Did you, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon feels like she knows the meaning of each individual word, but they stop making sense once you string them together into a sentence.

response.speaker: Arakunti
response.text: Why are the Golden Nara and the small flying thing here to find Arakunti?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon's not some small flying thing! Wait, Paimon actually is a flying... Argh! Anyway, Paimon's... Paimon!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Your "Golden Nara" also has a name, and that's {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Arapandu told us that you're in the Grove of Dreams and he sent us to check up on you.

response.speaker: Arakunti
response.text: You can tell Arapandu that Arakunti is fine, the Grove of Dreams is fine, and the humid dreams are also fine.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Okay... {NICKNAME}, let's head back and talk to Arapandu.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Or maybe not! We came here to heal the Varuna Contraption! That was close. Paimon was almost led by the nose...

response.speaker: Arakunti
response.text: You can tell Arapandu that Arakunti doesn't want to lead Paimon by the nose.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Arapandu probably doesn't want to know that.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon doesn't want to either! What on earth is going on with this Aranara!?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I recall Arapandu saying...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: He said, "Arakunti's more distant from Nara." Does that mean Arakunti doesn't know how to communicate with people?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Actually, we're the ones who don't know how to communicate with Aranara.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh! That's right... We're the ones who should try to follow the local customs and learn how to communicate with them.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But now that you mention it, how do Aranara communicate, anyway?

choices.text: What do you think, small flying thing?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If the Golden Nara doesn't know, what would the small flying thing know? Why don't we just ask the amazing Arakunti?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Can you tell us exactly how Aranara communicate with each other? We really wanna learn!

response.speaker: Arakunti
response.text: Why do you want to learn? Nara is Nara, Paimon is Paimon, and Aranara is Aranara.

response.speaker: Arakunti
response.text: Ah, Arakunti sees. Paimon also wants to turn into a seed and be buried in the soil?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No! Not at all!

response.speaker: Arakunti
response.text: Does the Golden Nara want to become a seed?

response.speaker: Arakunti
response.text: Too bad. Seeds are nice.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We've almost forgotten what we came here for. It's for Festival Utsava!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We need to heal the Varuna Contraption for Festival Utsava so that the weather will return to normal and there will be no more of those nasty spores.

response.speaker: Arakunti
response.text: Paimon is right. It's for the sake of Festival Utsava, and for the sake of the center of the blue earth.

response.speaker: Arakunti
response.text: A humid Grove of Dreams is good, but the "spores" are bad. The mushrooms that can run are bad too. There is also too much rain, so the mushrooms have become difficult to cook.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, see? You can be clear after all!

response.speaker: Arakunti
response.text: #We are going to heal the Varuna Contraption. Come with Arakunti, Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't talk nonsense, he'll think it's for real!

choices.text: Well, how about we start from using metaphors?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let Paimon try! The Golden Nara is just like... like... um... like a Teyvat Fried Egg?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Actually, let's just ask Arakunti directly.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Amazing! So what did his words mean?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: He said that he can transform into many other things.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Really? Don't you pull Paimon's leg, {NICKNAME}...

dialogues.speaker: Arakunti
dialogues.text: The roots of a big tree. Excellent. A wet breathing can be heard, a drowsy tune.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh... Paimon still can't understand what you're saying, Arakunti, but whatever!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Speaking of which, Paimon didn't think this place would be so large on the inside. Guess this is what they mean when they say "more than meets the eye," huh? Also, is it just Paimon, or does this place feel very different from other places?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are we going to look for the "leaves" that feed energy to the Varuna Contraption in a place like this...?

dialogues.speaker: Arakunti
dialogues.text: It's here, but it's not here. One can hear its voice, smell its breath, see its veins... But Paimon can't find it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? What was that about...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: If Paimon can't find it, then what about me?

dialogues.speaker: Arakunti
dialogues.text: The Golden Nara can see the melody, like the cool breeze of night, the sudden fall of a raindrop, the thousand dream-fragments of a lake's broken surface.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Well, that sure sounds impressive.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #As expected of {NICKNAME}!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hehe.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Hehe... Wait! You're stealing Paimon's line, {NICKNAME}!

dialogues.speaker: Arakunti
dialogues.text: #Nara {NICKNAME} turning into Paimon... is even scarier than dancing with mushrooms within Marana...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Can't imagine that...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's why this kind of thing won't happen! Best that it never does...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And Arakunti, can't you be more clear? Where in the world are we going to find the "leaves" of the Varuna Contraption?

dialogues.speaker: Arakunti
dialogues.text: In dreams.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait... Then why didn't you say so in the first place!?

dialogues.speaker: Arakunti
dialogues.text: Because you didn't ask "where" in the first place.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh... Paimon thinks that the Aranara way of communicating has hit her all of a sudden!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Arakunti, can you tell us where each of the three "leaves" we're looking for is located?

dialogues.speaker: Arakunti
dialogues.text: Yes.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, so you really only answer questions that are asked directly, huh... Okay, so where are these three locations?

dialogues.speaker: Arakunti
dialogues.text: Over here, over there, and on the other side.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh-huh... Wait, you're not describing anything!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Aaaand Paimon is defeated.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! Paimon's defeat is your defeat! They're the same thing! Arakunti's words can't be counted on... So how are we supposed to find those three locations?

dialogues.speaker: Arakunti
dialogues.text: The Varuna Contraption was made by the most remarkable Aranara, so the links between the "branch" and the "leaves" are invisible yet visible.

dialogues.speaker: Arakunti
dialogues.text: #Nara {NICKNAME} can see Aranara, and if you can see the traces of Aranara, you can find your way.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: P—Paimon can't believe she understood that!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We'll find it if we follow the trails of Aranara, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, come on, at least give Paimon the chance to answer this time, would you?

talks.objective: Play the Rhythm of the Great Dream in front of Silapna
Make the three "leaves" in the dream turn towards the "branch"

dialogues.speaker: Arakunti
dialogues.text: Humid dream, dry dream... Ding dong, tick tock, rustle... It's Vana's tune...

dialogues.speaker: Arakunti
dialogues.text: #Nara {NICKNAME}? The "leaves" are in the dream, and the "branch" is here.

talks.objective: Play the Rhythm of the Great Dream in front of Silapna

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're back!

dialogues.speaker: Arakunti
dialogues.text: Arakunti heard you. The whimpers have turned into a gentle tune, but to merge it into the great flow of sound, we still need...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We still need your help, Arakunti! Hehe, Paimon'll be counting on you!

dialogues.speaker: Arakunti
dialogues.text: Arakunti knows.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh! Then there shouldn't be any problems now, right? Paimon hopes we can heal the Varuna Contraption soon, or Apam Woods will be full of spores... Just thinking about it makes Paimon... Achoo!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon can't believe that you Aranara have no reaction to spores... How are you not affected at all?

dialogues.speaker: Arakunti
dialogues.text: Aranara are not unaffected. Aranara just cook mushrooms. But spores are too small and too many to catch.

dialogues.speaker: Arakunti
dialogues.text: When the Varuna Contraption wasn't broken, Vana didn't have so many mushrooms, so healing the Varuna Contraption could make everything better. Except Marana.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Things will surely get better.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, we'll help too!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We will find a way to deal with Marana too.

dialogues.speaker: Arakunti
dialogues.text: #Is Nara {NICKNAME} Nara Varuna?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Why are you asking that all of a sudden?

dialogues.speaker: Arakunti
dialogues.text: #Arapandu said that Nara Varuna was a golden, brave Nara. Together with Aranara, {F#he}{M#she} healed the Varuna Contraption, drove away the black rain and mud, and brought back the sun and moon.

dialogues.speaker: Arakunti
dialogues.text: #Nara {NICKNAME} has also helped Aranara to heal the Varuna Contraption, and you're a golden and brave Nara, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But isn't Nara Varuna someone from a long time ago...?

dialogues.speaker: Arakunti
dialogues.text: #Did Nara Varuna not return to Vana? Is Nara {NICKNAME} a completely different Nara?

dialogues.speaker: Arakunti
dialogues.text: Can different Nara have similar melodies?

response.speaker: Arakunti
response.text: #Arakunti has not met Nara Varuna, but Arapandu has talked a lot about {F#him}{M#her}.

response.speaker: Arakunti
response.text: #{F#His}{M#Her} melody must be the same as Nara {NICKNAME}'s. Listening to it will surely bring happiness.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Yeah, Paimon's always happy when she's with {NICKNAME}! If {NICKNAME} leaves Paimon one day, like Nara Varuna left the forest...

response.speaker: Arakunti
response.text: #Arapandu must be waiting for us at the "rest stop." Return with Arakunti, Nara {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right, let's head back!

choices.text: But I have something else to do.

response.speaker: Arakunti
response.text: It's okay, Arakunti can go back alone.
